entries.answer: I now have a comprehensive understanding of the entire technical document. It is the **Seedance 2.0** technical report by ByteDance Seed (arXiv:2604.14148v1). The document is primarily an evaluation/benchmark paper describing architecture, capabilities, training philosophy, and benchmarking of a unified multi-modal audio-video generation model. My task is to rewrite the entire content as a single, comprehensive, technical construction prompt — without naming the original model — in production-ready, unambiguous language.

Based on the full content of your uploaded technical report, here is the comprehensive, single, production-ready construction prompt:[1]

***

## Construction Prompt

Build a unified, large-scale, multi-modal audio-video joint generation model from scratch. The system must natively support four input modalities — text, image, audio, and video — and produce synchronized audio-video output. Every component described below must be implemented in complete, production-ready code with no placeholders, stubs, mock layers, or simplified approximations.

***

## 1. Overall Architecture

Design a single unified transformer-based diffusion architecture that jointly generates video and audio in one forward pass. The model must not treat video and audio as separate pipelines with a post-hoc fusion step. Instead, all modalities — text conditioning, image conditioning, video conditioning, audio conditioning, and the output video and audio streams — must be processed within one shared latent space and one shared set of transformer layers. The architecture must be highly efficient and scalable to large parameter counts.

The model must support the following generation tasks as first-class capabilities, all within the same weights:

- **Text-to-Video (T2V):** Generate a video clip with synchronized audio from a text prompt alone.
- **Image-to-Video (I2V):** Generate a video clip with synchronized audio conditioned on one or more reference images and an optional text prompt.
- **Reference-to-Video (R2V):** Generate a video clip conditioned on an arbitrary combination of up to 3 video clips, up to 9 images, and up to 3 audio clips simultaneously, along with a text prompt.
- **Video Editing:** Accept an existing video clip and a text instruction describing a targeted modification (subject replacement, style change, scene change, audio content change) and produce a modified video where non-targeted regions are preserved with maximum consistency.
- **Video Extension / Continuation:** Accept an existing video clip and generate a seamless forward or backward temporal continuation aligned with a user-provided text prompt. The continuation must be temporally coherent with the input clip, without visual discontinuities at the boundary.
- **Combination Tasks:** Support compound tasks that pair reference and editing within a single generation pass — for example, swapping the subject of an input video with a subject drawn from a reference image while preserving the scene, motion, and audio.

All tasks above must be executable in any standalone or combinatorial configuration using one model checkpoint, not separate fine-tuned checkpoints per task.

***

## 2. Output Specifications

The model must natively generate audio-video content with the following specifications:

- **Duration:** 4 to 15 seconds per generation.
- **Native output resolutions:** 480p and 720p.
- **Audio:** Binaural (dual-channel) stereo output. Multi-track: background audio, ambient sound effects, and character narration/dialogue must be generated simultaneously as separate tracks that are mixed into the final output with precise temporal alignment to the visual content.
- **Frame rate:** Standard cinematic/broadcast frame rates (24fps minimum; support 30fps).
- **Audio sample rate:** CD-quality minimum (44.1 kHz); professional-grade preferred (48 kHz).

***

## 3. Visual Tokenization and Latent Space

Implement a video variational autoencoder (VAE) that encodes raw video frames into a compressed spatiotemporal latent representation. The VAE must:

- Apply spatial and temporal downsampling to reduce the token count while preserving perceptually critical detail (fine textures, light refraction, facial micro-expressions, hand geometry).
- Produce a latent space in which both 480p and 720p videos of varying durations can be represented without architectural changes — use dynamic sequence length handling, not fixed-resolution heads.
- Achieve reconstruction quality sufficient that close-up shots of human faces, hands, fabric, and liquid surfaces are indistinguishable from real footage at the original resolution.
- Be jointly trained with the diffusion backbone or pre-trained and frozen, depending on the training recipe described in Section 7.

Implement a corresponding audio tokenizer / codec that encodes waveforms into a compact latent sequence compatible with the video latent in terms of temporal resolution and sequence length conventions. The audio latent must carry sufficient information to reconstruct the full binaural mix.

***

## 4. Multi-Modal Input Encoding

### 4.1 Text Encoder

Use a large pre-trained language model as the text encoder. The encoder must:

- Handle prompts of arbitrary length, including long multi-shot scripts with extensive character interaction descriptions, specific action sequences, camera movement directives, and stylistic aesthetic instructions.
- Preserve fine-grained semantic detail throughout the encoding — compound instructions, counter-factual instructions, and abstract creative prompts must all produce distinguishable conditioning signals.
- Support multilingual input including Chinese (standard Mandarin, Sichuan dialect, Northeastern dialect, Cantonese), Chinese opera, Chinese minority languages, English, and singing/rap content. The text encoder must not degrade on non-English input.

### 4.2 Image Encoder

Implement a visual feature extractor (e.g., a ViT-based encoder) that encodes reference images into dense visual feature sequences. The encoder must:

- Preserve subject identity, appearance details, artistic style, special effect style, and compositional layout of the reference image.
- When up to 9 reference images are provided simultaneously, encode each independently and provide all feature sequences to the main transformer via cross-attention or concatenation, without loss of per-image identity.

### 4.3 Video Reference Encoder

Implement encoding of reference video clips (up to 3 clips simultaneously). The encoder must extract and preserve:

- Subject appearance and identity across frames.
- Motion rhythm and temporal dynamics.
- Cinematographic properties: shot composition, camera movement trajectory, editing rhythm.
- Special effect visual styles and plot narrative structure.

### 4.4 Audio Reference Encoder

Implement encoding of reference audio clips (up to 3 clips simultaneously). The encoder must extract and preserve:

- Acoustic characteristics: timbre, prosody, singing style, instrumental texture.
- Temporal rhythm information for beat alignment with generated video.

***

## 5. Main Diffusion Transformer

The core generative module is a Diffusion Transformer (DiT) that operates in the joint audio-video latent space. Implement it as follows:

### 5.1 Architecture

- Use a full transformer backbone (not U-Net) operating on flattened spatiotemporal-audio latent token sequences.
- Implement 3D RoPE (Rotary Position Embedding) or an equivalent positional encoding that encodes spatial (height, width), temporal (frame index), and audio-temporal position jointly in a unified coordinate system.
- Implement adaptive layer normalization (adaLN) conditioned on diffusion timestep and all conditioning signals.
- All cross-modal conditioning (text, image features, video reference features, audio reference features) must be injected via cross-attention layers interleaved throughout the transformer depth. Do not inject conditioning only at the input or output layers.

### 5.2 Unified Joint Generation

The transformer must process video latent tokens and audio latent tokens as a single concatenated sequence, with attention operating across both modalities simultaneously. Audio-visual temporal alignment must emerge from this joint attention and must not require post-hoc synchronization.

### 5.3 Flow Matching / Score Matching Objective

Train the transformer using a continuous-time flow matching or score-based diffusion objective (e.g., rectified flow). Implement:

- A noise schedule appropriate for high-resolution spatiotemporal generation.
- Classifier-free guidance (CFG) for all conditioning signals independently, with separate guidance scales for text, image, video reference, and audio conditioning.
- Support for negative prompting.

### 5.4 Multi-Shot Native Generation

The architecture must inherently support multi-shot narrative generation without requiring external shot segmentation. The transformer must be capable of autonomously planning shot sequencing, designing transitions between shots, and maintaining subject identity across shots within a single generated clip. Implement positional encoding that enables this cross-shot consistency.

***

## 6. Audio Generation Module

Implement the audio generation module as a component integrated within the main transformer, not as a separate post-hoc system. Requirements:

- **Binaural spatial audio:** Generate true binaural (two-channel, head-related transfer function-aware) audio with spatial scene cues matching the visual content (e.g., sounds panning to match on-screen object positions).
- **Multi-track decomposition:** The generation must simultaneously produce: (1) background music/ambient audio, (2) environmental sound effects (footsteps, environmental sounds, physical interactions), and (3) character voice/dialogue/narration. These tracks must be temporally aligned with visual actions at the frame level.
- **Audio-visual synchronization:** Lip movements of on-screen characters must be synchronized with generated speech. Physical interactions (e.g., a hand hitting a surface) must produce sounds synchronized to the frame of contact. Beat matching between background music and visual editing rhythm must be enforced.
- **Voice and acoustic reference preservation:** When audio reference clips are provided, the generated audio must preserve the timbre, prosody, and vocal characteristics of the reference while adapting content to match the generated scene.

***

## 7. Training Pipeline

### 7.1 Data Pipeline

Build a large-scale data preprocessing pipeline for both video and audio:

- **Video data:** Ingest raw video at scale. Apply scene detection and shot segmentation. Filter for visual quality: resolution, compression artifacts, motion blur, occlusion. Apply aesthetic scoring to filter for cinematic quality, composition, and lighting. Generate dense captions for each clip using a multimodal vision-language model. Captions must describe: subjects and their appearances, actions, interactions, camera movements, lighting, composition, and style. Generate multilingual captions.
- **Audio data:** Separate audio tracks using source separation. Generate audio captions describing sound events, voice characteristics, music genre, and acoustic environment. Time-align audio event labels to video frame timestamps.
- **Multi-modal reference data:** Construct training samples that pair video clips with associated reference images, subject images, and audio clips to train the reference-conditioned generation capabilities. Construct editing pairs by applying transformations to source videos to produce (source, edit instruction, target) triplets for training the video editing capability. Construct extension pairs of consecutive clips for training video continuation.

### 7.2 Training Stages

Implement a multi-stage training recipe:

1. **Stage 1 — Large-scale pre-training:** Train the full model on text-to-video and image-to-video tasks at lower resolution (480p) using the full dataset. Establish strong foundational generation quality, motion naturalness, physics compliance, and basic instruction following.

2. **Stage 2 — High-resolution and joint audio-video training:** Continue training at 720p and introduce joint audio-video generation. The audio and video latents must be co-trained jointly at this stage, not sequentially.

3. **Stage 3 — Multi-modal reference and editing training:** Fine-tune on the reference-conditioned and editing datasets. Maintain a mixture of T2V/I2V samples to prevent degradation of foundational generation quality during this stage.

4. **Stage 4 — Alignment and quality tuning:** Apply a preference optimization or reward fine-tuning stage using human-preference data. Optimize for: motion naturalness, audio-visual sync, aesthetic quality, instruction-following accuracy, and physical plausibility. Use a realism study methodology: collect evaluator judgments on whether generated outputs are distinguishable from real video footage and use these labels as reward signal.

### 7.3 Loss Functions

Implement the following losses during training:

- Diffusion/flow matching denoising loss on both video and audio latent jointly.
- Consistency loss for editing tasks: penalize changes to non-targeted regions of the video during editing.
- Temporal consistency loss to enforce cross-frame coherence of subject appearance and scene geometry.
- Audio-visual synchronization loss: enforce temporal alignment between audio events and corresponding visual events.
- Reference fidelity loss: enforce that subject appearance, motion rhythm, and style in the generated output match the provided reference inputs.

***

## 8. Cinematographic and Directorial Reasoning

The model must not merely execute literal instructions — it must exhibit directorial reasoning capabilities:

- **Shot planning:** Given a long script or storyboard, the model must autonomously plan shot types (close-up, medium, wide, POV, crane, etc.), shot transitions, and editing rhythm without these being explicitly specified in the prompt.
- **Camera movement:** Support and accurately execute the following camera movements when instructed: dolly, zoom, pan, tilt, roll, rack focus, crane, handheld, steadicam. Support combined multi-axis movements.
- **Cinematographic rules:** The generated output must avoid 180-degree rule violations, redundant coverage, mismatched shot sizes within a scene, and uneven pacing unless such violations are explicitly requested.
- **Narrative coherence:** For abstract or vague prompts, the model must generate a coherent narrative interpretation rather than producing a sequence of loosely related images.

***

## 9. Evaluation Framework

Implement a comprehensive evaluation benchmark consisting of two tracks:

### 9.1 Objective Evaluation

Implement automated evaluation pipelines for:

- **Motion stability:** Measure subject deformation rate, structural integrity across frames, jitter, and temporal smoothness using optical flow-based and pose estimation-based metrics.
- **Prompt following accuracy:** Measure semantic alignment between prompt and output for each of the following fine-grained categories: holidays/festivals, consumer visual effects, counter-reality instructions, cinematic visual effects, same-type interaction, cross-type interaction, group coordinated motion, advanced camera movement, special camera shots, editing rhythm, combined shot instructions, physical feedback, physical phenomena, natural phenomena, text overlay, short text generation, creative text generation, long script execution, abstract challenges, multi-entity feature matching, knowledge assessment, compound multi-instructions, surreal motion, intense sports motion, fine hand motion, anthropomorphic motion, emotion and expression, visual style, lighting and color tone, framing and composition.
- **Aesthetic quality:** Automated aesthetic scoring for: visual style, lighting, composition, object material texture, character detail fidelity, costume/prop design quality.
- **Audio quality metrics:** Measure audio expressiveness, multi-track layer richness, melody/tone alignment with prompt context.
- **Audio-visual sync metrics:** Measure lip-sync accuracy, physical event sound offset (milliseconds), beat-match score between music and visual editing rhythm.
- **Generation consistency metrics for reference tasks:** Measure subject identity preservation (face similarity, clothing detail match), motion rhythm alignment, style transfer fidelity, scene preservation during editing.

### 9.2 Subjective Evaluation

Build a blind expert evaluation protocol:

- Recruit expert evaluators with professional background in advertising production and game/film production.
- Evaluate on a 1–5 rating scale for all dimensions listed in Section 9.1.
- Define usability rate as the fraction of outputs scoring ≥ 3, satisfaction rate as the fraction scoring ≥ 4, and delight rate as the fraction scoring 5.
- Run a realism study as a separate evaluation: present evaluators with interleaved real video clips and generated outputs and measure the model's ability to produce indistinguishable content.
- Evaluate narrative quality on three sub-dimensions: (1) cinematographic language — shot logic, expressiveness, absence of axis-crossing violations, matched shot sizing, even pacing; (2) plot design — coherence and engagement from vague prompts; (3) stylistic aesthetics — lighting, framing, composition, color grading, character/costume/prop/set consistency.

### 9.3 Evaluation Dataset Construction

Construct specialized evaluation datasets for each task group:

- Reference evaluation set: samples covering subject reference, motion reference, visual-effect reference, and style reference.
- Editing evaluation set: samples covering subject editing, style editing, scene editing, and audio content editing.
- Extension evaluation set: forward and backward plot continuation samples.
- Combination evaluation set: paired tasks representing real production workflows.
- Sample distribution within each set must be tuned to minimize evaluation variance at small sample budgets.

***

## 10. Inference and Fast Variant

### 10.1 Standard Inference

Implement DDIM-based or flow-matching ODE-based inference with configurable number of denoising steps. Support batched multi-sample generation. The inference pipeline must accept the full structured input (text prompt, up to 3 video reference clips, up to 9 image references, up to 3 audio reference clips) and produce a final muxed audio-video file.

### 10.2 Accelerated Fast Variant

Implement a distilled or otherwise accelerated variant of the model for low-latency scenarios. The fast variant must:

- Achieve substantially reduced inference time (target: 3–5× speedup over the standard model) through consistency distillation, step distillation, or another principled acceleration method.
- Maintain generation quality sufficient for production-grade use cases — quality degradation must be bounded and quantified.
- Share the same interface and input/output specification as the standard model. No separate preprocessing or postprocessing pipelines.

***

## 11. Safety Framework

Implement a structured safety assessment system integrated into the model lifecycle:

- **Pre-generation filtering:** Text and image prompt classifiers that detect and reject requests for: non-consensual intimate content, identifiable real persons in harmful scenarios, content depicting minors in unsafe contexts, and content violating applicable legal standards.
- **Post-generation filtering:** Video and audio classifiers applied to all model outputs before delivery. Flag and suppress outputs containing the above categories.
- **Iterative red-team evaluation:** Document a red-team evaluation protocol that is re-run at each training stage checkpoint and before each production deployment.
- **Bias and fairness audit:** Evaluate generated outputs for representation bias across gender, ethnicity, and age for all human-subject generation scenarios.

All safety components must be production-grade, not placeholder classifiers.

***

## 12. Deliverables

Deliver the following complete, unabridged, production-ready components with no omissions:

1. Full model architecture implementation (tokenizers, encoders, main DiT backbone, decoder, audio module) with all weights initialization and training code.
2. Full data preprocessing pipeline (video ingestion, quality filtering, captioning, audio separation, multi-modal pair construction, editing pair construction).
3. Full multi-stage training script with all loss functions, schedulers, and distributed training configuration.
4. Full inference pipeline supporting all task types (T2V, I2V, R2V, editing, extension, combination).
5. Full accelerated fast-variant distillation pipeline.
6. Full evaluation benchmark implementation (SeedVideoBench 2.0-equivalent) with all objective metric pipelines and subjective evaluation tooling.
7. Full safety filtering pipeline (pre- and post-generation classifiers).
8. Comprehensive test suite covering all generation task types, all input modality combinations, edge cases (empty reference sets, maximum reference counts, minimum and maximum duration), and all evaluation categories listed in Section 9.1.

Every file must be complete. No file may contain the string "TODO", "placeholder", "mock", "dummy", "stub", "simulated", "fake", or equivalent. All configuration values must be concrete and justified in inline documentation.
